page: Microsoft Azure D8plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing predictable compute performance without hyperthreading. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, and includes 307 GB of local storage alongside Premium Storage compatibility.

Benchmark evaluations place the D8plds_v5 in the average performance tier for multi-core operations, software compilation, and database tasks. The instance achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 6013.0 and a Clang compilation score of 9351.0. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached small-block reads at 565.84 GB/sec, though uncached large-block writes decrease to 43.64 GB/sec. Single-core performance and cryptographic execution are relatively weak, as shown by a Passmark CPU score of 6130.18 and a weak encryption test result of 1295.58, partly due to the absence of advanced vector and matrix extensions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture offers a resource-dense profile for scale-out workloads that do not require massive memory allocations. The inclusion of 307 GB of local storage provides a built-in storage buffer without requiring external attachments. This server type is well-suited for web serving, application servers, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and lightweight database operations, but is less optimal for memory-intensive applications or large language model inference.
